McLean County sits in western Kentucky along the Green River. Calhoun is the county seat, and Livermore is the largest city. This guide explains how McLean County, Kentucky tax lien certificates work. It covers sale timing, registration, location, returns, risks, and post sale steps. McLean County says unpaid tax bills move from the Sheriff to the County Clerk after mid April, then the Clerk runs a tax sale before the end of August.

What Are McLean County, Kentucky Tax Lien Certificates?

McLean County sells certificates of delinquency, not tax deeds. A buyer pays a delinquent tax bill. In return, the buyer receives a tax lien certificate. The owner can pay the debt, interest, and allowed fees. If the bill stays unpaid, the buyer may later use a court process to collect or foreclose. Kentucky sets the certificate interest rate at 12 percent simple interest per year.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • McLean County, Kentucky, conducts tax lien sales for delinquent tax certificates, with typical sales held in late August.
  • Investors can earn a fixed 12 percent interest per year on these tax lien certificates, offering high return potential.
  • Registration with the County Clerk is mandatory, and buyers must submit their lists at least 10 days before the sale.
  • Careful due diligence is essential to minimize risks, as tax lien certificates do not equate to property ownership immediately.
  • McLean County is open to all investors, including foreign buyers, but they should consult with the Clerk for specific requirements.

Fun Facts About McLean County

  • McLean County has about 9,000 residents, based on Census estimates.
  • Calhoun sits on the north bank of the Green River.
  • Livermore sits near the meeting point of the Green and Rough Rivers.
  • The county has a rural land base, small towns, and local river history.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions: Myer Creek Park offers trails, pavilions, riding areas, picnic sites, and historic log structures.
  • Outdoor life: county tourism points to golf, fishing, water skiing, disc golf, and horseback riding.
  • Transportation: US 431 runs through McLean County, with KY routes serving local towns.
  • Economy: farming, small retail, local services, and river area travel support the county.

Why Is McLean County Good for Tax Lien Investors?

  • McLean County tax lien certificates can offer high returns through a fixed 12 percent yearly rate.
  • The lien process can be a low risk investment when buyers research each parcel first.
  • Smaller counties may have fewer bidders than larger metro markets.
  • Kentucky rules create clear state tax lien opportunities for patient buyers.
  • The best edge is careful parcel review, not speed.

Auction Process for McLean County Tax Lien Sales

McLean County uses the Kentucky certificate of delinquency process. This is not a tax deed sale. It is also not a normal bid down interest auction. Kentucky sets the interest rate by law. Buyers register, submit lists, pay fees, and take part in a selection process. The County Clerk uses priority claims first. Then buyers select from current year certificates through rounds. The state guide says the selection order comes from a random drawing.

How the Auction Works

  1. Check the list.

    Review the McLean County delinquent tax list on the Clerk site or approved listing site.

  2. Register early.

    All buyers must register with the County Clerk. Some buyers must also register with the Kentucky Department of Revenue.

  3. Submit your lists.

    Buyers submit any priority certificate list and current year purchase list before the deadline.

  4. Pay the deposit.

    McLean County’s form calls for full deposit on priority certificates and 25 percent on current certificates.

  5. Attend the sale.

    Registered buyers report to the Clerk office. The McLean County form lists the Clerk office at 210 Main Street, Calhoun, Kentucky.

  6. Select certificates.

    Buyers pick certificates in rounds based on the sale order.

  7. Pay the balance.

    After the sale, the buyer pays the balance, filing fees, and allowed charges.

Registration Rules for McLean County Tax Sales

Yes, registration is required. McLean County posts forms for third party purchaser registration on its delinquent tax page.

State registration is also required if a buyer plans to buy more than three certificates in one county, more than five statewide, or invest more than $10,000. The state also uses a 60 day waiting period after it receives the application. County registration is separate. The state says each county clerk advertises local deadlines at least 30 days before the sale.

For McLean County, the county form says registration forms, lists, fees, and deposits must reach the Clerk at least 10 calendar days before the sale.

Maximum Returns and Expected Returns on McLean County Certificates

The maximum base return comes from Kentucky law. A certificate earns 12 percent simple interest per year. That equals about 1 percent per month, with partial months counted as a full month.

Expected returns depend on when the owner pays. A fast payoff means less interest. A slow payoff may mean more interest, but it also adds time and work. Buyers may also face notice rules, record checks, and court costs. According to our analysis, McLean County rewards careful buyers who value clean records over volume.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

Kentucky rules do not limit tax lien buyers to McLean County residents. They focus on registration, fees, deposits, and proper buyer conduct. That means local, out of county, and international investors may review the process. Foreign investor participation can work, but buyers should ask the Clerk about forms, payment methods, and mailing needs before the sale. They should also speak with a tax pro about United States tax reporting.

Importance of Due Diligence in McLean County Tax Lien Investing

Due diligence means checking the property before you buy the lien. A tax lien certificate is not the same as owning the property. You are buying a debt claim secured by the property.

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check the PVA record and parcel map.
  • Review Clerk records for deeds, mortgages, and other liens.
  • Drive by the property when allowed.
  • Check flood, access, and condition risk.
  • Estimate payoff odds and legal costs.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • The property may have poor access.
  • The land may be low value.
  • The owner may file bankruptcy.
  • Other liens may slow resale.
  • A court case may cost more than expected.

Buying Over the Counter Liens in McLean County

How to Purchase OTC Liens

Kentucky allows remaining certificates to be purchased after the tax sale. The state guide says unsold certificates may be bought later by third party buyers who still meet registration rules. A $10 per certificate county registration fee may apply until the yearly cap is reached.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

OTC tax liens can help buyers avoid sale day pressure. The interest rate stays set by law. You still need research. Unsold liens may have more risk, so review each parcel with care.

Why Is McLean County a Top Choice for Tax Lien Investors?

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • McLean County sits in the Green River area of western Kentucky.
  • Small county sales may have less crowd pressure.
  • The state rate is clear and fixed.
  • Local records sit with the County Clerk and PVA.
  • The county’s rural base can create lower entry points.

Real Estate Market Overview

McLean County is a small rural market. That can help patient lien buyers. Many parcels may be homes, farms, lots, or small town properties. Demand may not move as fast as larger cities. That is why price, access, and owner payoff odds matter more here.

Conclusion

McLean County, Kentucky tax lien certificates are best for patient investors. The county sells certificates of delinquency, not tax deeds. The typical sale window is late August. The sale has used 8:00 a.m. Central Time at the McLean County Clerk’s Office in Calhoun. Buyers must register before the deadline, submit purchase lists, and meet deposit rules.

The main benefit is the 12 percent simple yearly interest rate set by Kentucky law. The main risk is poor research. Always check the property, title records, access, and payoff chance before you buy. Smart investing starts before sale day.

Pro Tips for McLean County Tax Lien Investors

  • Call the Clerk before the sale and confirm the current local deadline.
  • Build a short list, then rank parcels by value and access.
  • Focus on parcels near Calhoun, Livermore, and known road routes.
  • Check Green River area flood risk before you buy.
  • Do not buy only because the tax bill is small.

McLean County Tax Lien FAQs

Can I renovate right after buying a lien?

No. A certificate is a lien. It is not ownership.

Do I need quiet title after foreclosure?

Often yes. Ask a Kentucky real estate attorney before resale.

Who handles occupants after a deed is issued?

The new owner must follow court and eviction rules.

Can I finance a tax lien purchase?

Some buyers use private funds, but the Clerk controls payment rules.

Can I resell the property right away?

Only after you gain lawful title and clear title issues.
